content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge treats the Acts 2:30 dispute as a clash between the defender's and challenger's chains and resolves it as underdetermined rather than requiring a single contrary verse.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "none", "why": "The judge compares the two chains and declares the issue underdetermined because neither forces the other, without imposing a single-verse contrary test."}
